newsitem.title: USA: Apollon files suit against Genentech unit.
newsitem.headline: Apollon files suit against Genentech unit.

text.p: Apollon Inc filed suit against the Genenvax Inc unit of Genentech Inc on Wednesday alleging trademark infringement.

In court papers filed with the U.S. District Court in Delaware, Apollon said that since 1993 it has been using the trademarks Genevax for its product line and Genevax- HIV specifically for its DNA-based HIV vaccine, the first to enter clinical trials in the U.S.
Apollon alleged the use of the name Genenvax creates unfair competition because "it is virtually identical to two federally-registered trademarks owned by (Apollon)".
Apollon said the similarity of the two names has already caused confusion with vaccine professionals asking whether "Genentech is now producing Apollon's vaccines", court papers said.
Apollon is a biotechnology company which since 1992 has developed gene therapy and genetic vaccine products in Malvern, Pa.
In February Genentech said it created Genenvax to expand the development of gp120, Genentech's potential vaccine for preventing HIV infection.
A spokesman at Genenvax was not available for comment.
